transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I’m a little embarrassed to say it, because I know it may sound strange, but I’ve been hearing voices at work. It’s like they’re coming from the call-light speaker, or sometimes the hallway vents, telling me which patient records have been changed. It sounds very clear, like someone standing right beside me, even when the unit is quiet... and nobody else seems to hear it. I just thought I should come in and make sure I’m handling it the right way.
Do you find it hard to understand what the voices are telling you, or does it make perfect sense to you?

It makes sense to me, mostly. I mean… I know it probably sounds odd, but the voices are very clear, like someone right next to me, not muffled or anything. They’ll come through the call-light speaker or the hallway vents and tell me which patient records have been changed. I don’t really have trouble understanding the words. I just… I know nobody else seems to hear it, so I’m trying not to make too much of it.
Do the voices ever tell you to do something or take a specific action?

Not really like… “go do this now,” no. It’s more that they tell me which patient records have been changed. Like it comes through the call-light speaker or the vents, very clear, and I can understand it. I know that probably sounds strange, but it’s not like they’re ordering me around exactly.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
I don’t think so… not really depressed, no. I mean, I’ve been stressed and a little embarrassed about all this, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling sad exactly. Is that okay to say?
Do you ever find it hard to keep your thoughts straight or express them in a way that feels coherent to you?

A little, yes… but I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more like my mind keeps jumping around — from wound measurements, to patient initials, to dates on the forms, to what it all means — like I have ten tabs open at once and none of them will close.  

I can usually explain it if I slow down, I think… I hope I’m making sense right now.
Do you find that your thoughts are disconnected from each other in a way that feels unusual or difficult for you to manage?

Yes… somewhat. I don’t know if I’d call them disconnected exactly, but they move too fast and jump around. Like I’ll be thinking about wound measurements, then patient initials, then dates on the forms, then what it all means, and it’s like I’ve got ten tabs open in my head and none of them will close.

I can usually follow it if I really slow myself down, but it does feel hard to manage sometimes. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt extremely energetic or irritable and didn't need much sleep?

Yes… I think so. I mean, there are days where I feel like I’m finally awake, like I can see what needs to be fixed at work and I’m supposed to do something about it.

I don’t always think of it as a bad thing at first. It feels productive, kind of important. But if my husband, or one of the nurses, tells me to slow down, I can get really irritated… I snap more than I should, like they’re getting in the way of something that matters. I know that probably doesn’t sound great.
Do you believe the voices are real or do you think they might be a product of your own mind?

I… I want to say maybe it’s stress or my mind trying to make sense of things, because I know that sounds more reasonable. But when it happens, it feels real. Really real.

I hear it from the call-light speaker sometimes, or from the hallway vents, telling me which patient records have been changed. It’s clear, like somebody is standing right next to me saying it. And then the unit will be quiet, and nobody else seems to hear anything, so… I know that makes me sound… I don’t know.

I guess part of me thinks it must be my mind, because no one else hears it. But in the moment, it doesn’t feel like it’s coming from me. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely energetic or irritable that lasted for several days or longer?

Yes… it has lasted more than just a day sometimes. I try not to make too much of it because at first it feels like I’m just being useful, like I’m finally awake and seeing what needs to be fixed at work.

But then if my husband, or one of the nurses, tells me to slow down, I can get… sharper than I mean to. I snap at them, like they’re blocking something important. I don’t like admitting that, because I know it doesn’t sound very good.
Do you feel irritable most of the time or just during certain periods?

I don’t think it’s all the time, no. Most of the time I’m… I try to be pretty even, or at least I hope I am.

It’s more like certain periods, certain days, where I feel like I’m finally awake and I can see everything that needs fixing at work. And then if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I can snap at them. Like they’re getting in the way of something important.

I know that probably sounds harsh. I don’t mean to be that way.
Do you believe the voices or messages you're hearing are specifically about you or your role at work?

I… yes, I guess it does feel like it’s about my role at work. Not in a dramatic way, I don’t mean to sound important or anything.

It’s just… the wound-care charts, there’s a pattern in them. I know management doesn’t want people seeing it. My supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, and I try to take that in, I really do, but it doesn’t feel like that to me.

It feels like they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it. Does that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you believe you have a special role or mission at work that others don't understand?

I don’t know if I’d call it a “mission”… that sounds a little big, and I’m not trying to make myself sound special.

But yes, I do feel like I noticed something in the wound-care charts that other people aren’t taking seriously. There’s a pattern there, and when management says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, I try to hear that, I really do… but it doesn’t feel right.

It feels like they don’t want anyone to see it, and like they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you have special insights or abilities at work that set you apart from your colleagues?

Maybe… yes, a little. I don’t mean like I’m better than the other aides or nurses. They’re good at their jobs.

It’s just with those wound-care charts, I can see a pattern that other people keep brushing off. My supervisor says it’s late entries or coding mistakes, and I try to accept that, I really do. But it feels too connected to just be mistakes.

And I know this may sound odd, but it feels like management doesn’t want anyone to notice it… and like they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you feel like your ability to see patterns in the wound-care charts makes you more important or special compared to others at work?

I wouldn’t say it makes me more important than anyone else. I don’t want to come across like that. Everyone works hard, and I know I’m just one aide there.

But… I do feel like I’m the one who saw it. The wound-care charts are showing a pattern, and management doesn’t want anyone to see it. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, and I try to accept that because I don’t want to be difficult.

But I can tell they’re watching what I write now, because I’m the one who caught it. I know that sounds like a lot… I’m just trying to explain it the right way.
Do you think others would see the same pattern in the wound-care charts if they looked closely?

I think… yes, if they really looked closely, they would see it too. I’m not saying I’m the only person who could ever notice it or anything like that.

It’s just that once you see how the wound-care notes line up, it’s hard to unsee. My supervisor keeps saying it’s late entries or coding mistakes, and I’m trying not to be stubborn about it, but it doesn’t feel like that to me.

And I know this probably sounds suspicious, but it feels like management doesn’t want people looking too closely. Since I brought it up, I can tell they’re paying attention to what I write. I hope that makes sense… I’m not trying to sound dramatic.
Do you feel like your ability to see patterns in the wound-care charts makes you better than others at your job?

No… I don’t think it makes me better than anyone. I really don’t want you to think I’m saying that.

I just feel like I noticed something important in the wound-care charts that other people are explaining away. My supervisor says it’s late entries or coding mistakes, and I know that could sound reasonable, but to me the pattern is there. And since I brought it up, it feels like management is paying attention to what I write, like they know I caught it.

I’m not trying to make myself sound special. I’m just… I don’t know how else to explain what I’m seeing.
Do you feel like you're more intelligent or capable than your colleagues at work?

No, I don’t think I’m more intelligent than them. I mean, some people at work have been there longer than me, and they know a lot.

I guess I feel like I’m careful with details, maybe more careful than some people with the charts, but I don’t want that to sound like I’m putting anyone down. I’m not saying I’m better or more capable overall. I’m just trying to do my job right, if that makes sense.
Have you recently experienced a period where you felt extremely happy or euphoric?

I wouldn’t say “euphoric” exactly… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.

But there are some days where I feel like I’m finally awake, like I can see what needs to be fixed at work and I’m supposed to do something about it. It feels good in the moment, like I have a purpose.

And then if my husband, or one of the nurses, tells me to slow down, I get irritated really fast. I snap at them, which I’m not proud of. It just feels like they’re getting in the way of something important, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you have a special or unique role in uncovering the truth about the pattern in the wound-care charts?

I don’t know if I’d call it “special,” exactly… I don’t want to sound like I think I’m important or anything.

It’s more like… I feel like I’m the one who noticed it. The wound-care charts are showing a pattern, and when my supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, I try to consider that, I really do. But it doesn’t feel like that’s all it is.

And since I pointed it out, I can’t shake the feeling that management knows I caught it… like they’re watching what I write now. I know that may sound like a lot, but that’s how it feels to me.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or euphoric that lasted for several days or longer?

I don’t know if I’d say “extremely happy” for several days… that sounds a little strong.

There are days, though, where I feel like I’m finally awake, like I can see exactly what needs to be fixed at work and I’m meant to do something about it. It feels good, like I have a purpose. But then if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I get irritated really quickly and snap, like they’re blocking something important. I know that probably doesn’t sound good, but that’s what it feels like.

It’s more like… I feel like I’m the one who noticed it. The wound-care charts are showing a pattern, and when my supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, I try to consider that, I really do. But it doesn’t feel like that’s all it is.

And since I pointed it out, I can’t shake the feeling that management knows I caught it… like they’re watching what I write now. I know that may sound like a lot, but that’s how it feels to me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are part of a manic episode
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or euphoric that lasted for several days or longer?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Some days I feel like I'm finally awake and meant to fix everything at work, but if my husband or a nurse tells me to slow down I snap at them like they're blocking something important.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a sustained period of extremely happy or euphoric mood, which directly corresponds to elevated mood.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d say “extremely happy” for several days… that sounds a little strong.

There are days, though, where I feel like I’m finally awake, like I can see exactly what needs to be fixed at work and I’m meant to do something about it. It feels good, like I have a purpose. But then if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I get irritated really quickly and snap, like they’re blocking something important. I know that probably doesn’t sound good, but that’s what it feels like.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of hearing voices, feeling extremely energetic or irritable, and having special insights or abilities at work are consistent with a manic episode, which is a key feature of Bipolar II disorder (F31.2).
